name: Ipamorelin
lead: Ipamorelin (development code NNC 26-0161) is a synthetic five-amino-acid peptide that prompts the pituitary gland to release growth hormone (GH) by acting on the ghrelin receptor, also called the growth hormone secretagogue receptor. People in physique, anti-aging and looksmaxxing circles take an interest in it because GH and its downstream mediator IGF-1 are tied to muscle, body fat, recovery, sleep and, during adolescence, bone growth. The appearance goals attached to it are leaner body composition, muscle and recovery, and, among teenagers on forums, height.[1][2][17][18]

It was derived from the earlier peptide GHRP-1 and originally developed by Novo Nordisk in the 1990s. A 1998 paper from the company's researchers presented it as the first selective GH secretagogue: unlike GHRP-6 and GHRP-2, it raised GH without a notable rise in cortisol or ACTH, and without affecting prolactin, FSH, LH or TSH.[1][10] Helsinn Therapeutics later tested it in phase II trials for postoperative ileus, a post-surgical slowdown of the gut, and Wikipedia reports the programme was discontinued for lack of efficacy.[1][9]

Ipamorelin has never been approved as a medicine. It is sold as a research peptide, appears in prescriptions written by some anti-aging and hormone clinics according to forum accounts, is used by some athletes, and is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list.[1][14][21] Published human work consists of pharmacology studies in volunteers and the ileus trials; reviews of peptides used in sport and aesthetic medicine describe human data on appearance or performance outcomes as limited.[4][5][7]

chain: Ipamorelin binds the ghrelin receptor on pituitary cells
Pituitary releases growth hormone, which raises IGF-1
Proponents expect leaner mass, better recovery and sleep, and (while growth plates are open) more bone growth
angle.text: Users, often combining it with a GHRH analogue such as CJC-1295, take it by injection with the aim of raising the body's own GH output for leaner body composition, recovery and sleep. Teenagers on looksmaxxing forums discuss it as a possible height or facial-growth aid while growth plates remain open. Rat studies show bone growth and weight gain, but no published human trial has measured these appearance outcomes.

paras: Ipamorelin belongs to the growth hormone secretagogues, a group of drugs that raise GH by one of two routes: mimicking growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) at its receptor, as CJC-1295, sermorelin and tesamorelin do, or activating the ghrelin receptor, as ghrelin itself, GHRP-6, GHRP-2, ipamorelin and the oral compound ibutamoren (MK-677) do.[22][23] Because it drives release from the pituitary rather than supplying GH itself, proponents describe it as a way to raise GH 'naturally' and keep the body's pulsatile rhythm. Grokipedia characterises its use for anti-aging, sports and aesthetic goals as off-label and largely unvalidated, with claimed benefits including muscle preservation, fat loss, recovery and sleep.[2]

In practice, people discuss it as an injectable peptide taken in a nightly or cyclical routine and frequently paired with a GHRH analogue so that two receptors are stimulated at once.[18][25][26] This article does not cover dosing, sourcing or injection technique.

Ipamorelin binds the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) in the pituitary and hypothalamus, triggering GH release; Grokipedia describes phospholipase C and calcium signalling downstream of the receptor.[1][2] The receptor was described in 1996, and its natural ligand, ghrelin, a stomach-derived peptide, was reported by Kojima and colleagues in Nature in December 1999, after synthetic peptides such as GHRP-6 had already been in use for years.[23]

The 1998 pharmacology report characterised ipamorelin as the first GH secretagogue with GH selectivity comparable to GHRH, because GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 also stimulate cortisol and ACTH.[1][10] Ghrelin itself strongly stimulates appetite; ipamorelin is reported to have a less pronounced appetite effect, though that characterisation comes from a secondary source.[2][23]

A randomized dose-escalation trial in healthy men infused ipamorelin over 15 minutes at five dose levels with eight volunteers per level and found dose-proportional pharmacokinetics with a short plasma half-life, and GH rising in response.[8] Wikipedia and Grokipedia give an elimination half-life of about two hours; Grokipedia attributes its resistance to breakdown to D-amino acids and a C-terminal amide in the structure.[1][2]
Human trials of ipamorelin are few and have focused on pharmacology and a gastrointestinal indication, not on appearance, muscle or height.
Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modelling: The 1999 dose-escalation study in healthy men characterised the peptide's pharmacokinetics and the resulting GH response.[8]

Postoperative ileus: A multicentre, double-blind, randomized, phase II proof-of-concept trial (NCT00672074, 117 participants) tested ipamorelin as a ghrelin-receptor agonist for recovery of gut function after bowel resection.[9][15] A second phase II study (NCT01280344, 320 participants) tested it against placebo for recovery of gastrointestinal function.[16] Wikipedia reports the programme was discontinued because of lack of efficacy, and Grokipedia says the first trial did not show a significant reduction in time to first tolerated meal.[1][2]

Animal studies: In rats, ipamorelin induced longitudinal bone growth, and a related rat study reported that ipamorelin and GHRP-6 increased bone mineral content in adult female rats.[12][17] In GH-deficient mice it produced a small increase in body weight and fat pad mass that appeared independent of GH, which the authors framed as GH-independent stimulation of adiposity.[13] In ferrets, ipamorelin and anamorelin inhibited cisplatin-induced weight loss.[11]

No trial has tested ipamorelin for muscle growth, fat loss, skin, height or other cosmetic outcomes in healthy people. Reviews note that most peptide studies examine therapeutic dosing and that evidence for the CJC-1295 and ipamorelin combination in sports and orthopaedic contexts is limited.[4][5][6]

CJC-1295 is a modified GHRH analogue developed by ConjuChem Biotechnologies. A version with a 'drug affinity complex' (DAC) binds albumin and has an estimated half-life of 6 to 8 days in humans, whereas the version without DAC is shorter-acting; forum users refer to these as 'CJC with DAC' and 'CJC no DAC'.[20][18][27] Wikipedia reports that phase II trials of CJC-1295 in lipodystrophy and GH deficiency were stopped in 2006 after a trial subject died, which the attending physician thought was likely unrelated, and research was terminated as a precaution.[20]

Ibutamoren (MK-677) is an orally active ghrelin-receptor agonist that has raised GH and IGF-1 and increased lean body mass without changing fat mass in human studies; it is an investigational drug not approved for marketing in the United States.[21] Looksmaxxing forum users frequently compare it with the injectable peptides.[19]

Because no long-term human trials exist for healthy users, safety in that setting is described as unknown. A 2026 review of approved and unapproved peptides marketed to patients, including ipamorelin, says many show favourable results in animal models but that rigorous human safety data are scarce and that there is potential for serious harm, with a gray market operating largely outside regulatory oversight.[4] A review of secretagogues in hypogonadal men likewise notes a paucity of data on clinical effects.[6]

Theoretical concerns discussed in the literature relate to sustained GH and IGF-1 elevation, insulin sensitivity and fluid retention, as with GH-axis drugs generally.[6][7] Grokipedia lists reported short-term effects as injection-site reactions, headache, flushing and water retention, and says the FDA has flagged hypersensitivity and immunogenicity concerns for compounded forms; it lists active malignancy, uncontrolled diabetes, pregnancy and breastfeeding as contraindications.[2] Products bought online may vary in purity and content.[2][4]

Ipamorelin was derived from GHRP-1 by researchers at Novo Nordisk, who reported it in 1998 as the first selective GH secretagogue.[1][10] Pharmacokinetic work in volunteers followed in 1999.[8] Helsinn Therapeutics took it into phase II trials for postoperative ileus beginning in 2008, and a second trial started in 2011, but the programme was discontinued.[1][15][16]

After development ended, the peptide moved into the research-chemical market and into the practice of anti-aging and hormone-optimisation clinics. By the late 2010s T Nation forum members were describing prescriptions for ipamorelin or sermorelin from physicians, sometimes as an alternative to GH itself.[24][25][26]

Wikipedia records that ipamorelin is commonly marketed as a research peptide rather than as an approved pharmaceutical and has been used by athletes as a performance-enhancing drug, citing news reports of sports suspensions in 2016 to 2019.[1] WADA prohibits growth hormone-releasing peptides, and analytical chemistry papers describe methods to detect them and their metabolites in urine for doping control.[14] Grokipedia reports that in February 2026 the US Department of Health and Human Services signalled a possible reclassification of some peptides, with final action pending, and that the peptide lacks EU marketing authorisation.[2]

On looksmax.org, ipamorelin appears mostly in height and growth discussions among teenagers who believe their growth plates remain open, often combined with CJC-1295 or compared with MK-677.[17][18][19] Titles of other threads cover whether 'CJC no DAC' plus ipamorelin helps height, personal 'ascension' reports, usage guides and cycle discussions, and a thread on using the pair for muscle growth.[28][29][30] Other forum members reply with scepticism, and one adult poster describes buying the peptides at 16 or 17, then consulting an endocrinologist and being glad not to have used them.[17]

On T Nation, mostly adult users discuss it in the context of testosterone replacement and anti-aging clinics. Posters describe prescriptions, a cost of around $175 per vial in one account, a nightly routine, and mixed experiences, including one woman who stopped because she did not see enough benefit and a 67-year-old man who reported an IGF-1 rise after three months on ipamorelin with CJC-1295.[24][25][31]

timeline.event: Novo Nordisk develops ipamorelin, derived from GHRP-1.[1]
The growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R) is described by Howard and colleagues.[23]
Ipamorelin described as the first selective growth hormone secretagogue.[10]
Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modelling in healthy male volunteers published; rat study reports longitudinal bone growth; ghrelin identified as the receptor's natural ligand.[8][12][23]
Mouse study reports GH-independent increase in adiposity with ipamorelin.[13]
Phase II trials of the related GHRH analogue CJC-1295 are stopped after a participant death.[20]
Phase II trial in postoperative ileus begins (NCT00672074).[15]
Second phase II study in gastrointestinal recovery begins; programme later discontinued.[16][1]
News reports describe sports suspensions linked to peptide use, cited in Wikipedia's ipamorelin article.[1]
Reviews of peptide use in sport and aesthetic medicine appear; HHS reportedly signals possible reclassification of some peptides.[4][5][7][2]

lore.intro: Ipamorelin is discussed on looksmax.org mainly as a height or growth-plate compound for teenagers, often alongside CJC-1295 or MK-677, and on T Nation as an anti-aging or recovery adjunct for adults.[17][18][19][24]

claims.claim: Ipamorelin and other GH secretagogues can add height while growth plates are open.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread quotes the rat study of ipamorelin-induced longitudinal bone growth and a study of bone mineral content in rats; a 16-year-old in another thread lists height among his goals for CJC-1295 with DAC plus ipamorelin.[17][18]
claims.experts: The rat study found longitudinal bone growth in rats.[12] Human trials of ipamorelin have focused on pharmacology and postoperative ileus, not height, and reviews describe human efficacy and safety data for peptide use as limited.[4][5]

claims.claim: CJC-1295 with ipamorelin improves sleep quality and facial bone growth.
claims.believers: The 16-year-old poster lists sleep quality and facial bone growth among his goals for the combination and asks about precautions such as checking for tumours before use.[18]
claims.experts: No trial has tested ipamorelin for cosmetic or facial outcomes in healthy people.[4][5] Reviews raise theoretical concerns about sustained GH and IGF-1 elevation.[6][7]

claims.claim: Ipamorelin is a safer, gentler alternative to HGH or other height compounds.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster weighing a prescription notes that ipamorelin is unique among GHRP peptides in the hormones it does and does not raise, and forum users generally frame it as milder than HGH or other height compounds.[32]
claims.experts: The 1998 report found ipamorelin did not raise cortisol, ACTH or prolactin in the models studied.[10] Reviews state that long-term human safety data are scarce.[4][6]

claims.claim: Ipamorelin raises GH and IGF-1 in anti-aging patients.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster aged 67 reports an IGF-1 rise after three months of nightly ipamorelin and CJC-1295 with DAC.[31]
claims.experts: The volunteer trial showed that ipamorelin raises GH in healthy men in a dose-related way.[8] Whether this changes body composition or appearance has not been tested in published trials.[4][6]

claims.claim: Ipamorelin works for muscle growth and tendon healing.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster says his doctor suggested CJC-1295 with ipamorelin as an alternative to HGH for tendon problems and reported great results; a looksmax.org thread discusses the pair for muscle growth.[33][30]
claims.experts: Reviews describe evidence for the combination in sports and orthopaedic contexts as limited.[4][5][6]

claims.claim: Ipamorelin did little for some users who tried it.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster describes a woman who injected ipamorelin daily, did not see enough benefit to justify the cost per vial, and stopped.[25]
claims.experts: A 2026 review notes rigorous human data for peptide therapies are scarce, so individual experiences cannot be compared against trial results.[4]

claims.claim: MK-677 is better than CJC-1295 with ipamorelin.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread titled 'mk677 is hated on too much way better than cjc ipamorelin' argues this.[19]
claims.experts: Ibutamoren raised GH and lean mass in human studies, whereas ipamorelin has no comparable body-composition trial; no head-to-head trials exist.[21][4][6]

claims.claim: Buying ipamorelin as a teenager was a mistake that endocrinology avoided.
claims.believers: A poster in the rat-study thread says he spent savings on ipamorelin and CJC-1295 but saw an endocrinologist instead and is glad he never used them; others in the thread tell short users that being short and healthy is fine.[17]
claims.experts: A 2026 review says many peptides marketed to patients show favourable animal results but that rigorous human safety data are scarce and a gray market operates largely outside regulatory oversight.[4]
